title: Audit-first admin toggles: data offboarding lock, network access lists, and public-link blockade
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a trio of admin controls focused on compliance: a reversible Data Offboarding Lock (prevents bulk data egress), Network Access Lists (tenant-scoped allowlist for egress and UI/API access), and a Public-Link Blockade (disable creation of shareable public links). All toggles must be audit-first: every change emits structured audit events, integrates with RBAC v2 roles, and is respected by hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Admin console exposes three toggles with explanatory copy and links to policies
Toggle state changes produce structured audit log entries with actor, timestamp, previous_state, target_scope, and reason
RBAC v2 role mapping allows granular permission (view, modify, override) per toggle
API surfaces CRUD for toggle configs, with strict IAM checks and request-level logging
Network Access Lists enforce at control plane and runtime routing layers for hosted and dedicated
Data Offboarding Lock blocks: bulk export endpoints, admin-triggered offload jobs, and connector exports until unlocked
Public-Link Blockade prevents generation of ephemeral public URLs and removes existing public links when enabled
E2E tests simulate tenant with mixed-role users to validate enforcement across UI, API, and SDKs
Telemetry shows toggle adoption and any blocked export attempts with tenant ID and rule matched
technical_design: We are adding a scoped compliance flag object to the config service (scoped by org -> team -> project). Flags: data_offboard_lock (boolean), network_access_list (list of CIDR or cloud-region identifiers), public_link_block (boolean). The config service emits events to the audit bus on change. Runtime enforcers (gateway, runtime router, and export worker) subscribe and cache flags via immutable versioned view. RBAC v2 will introduce three granular permissions per flag: viewing the flag, changing the flag, and creating exceptions. Exceptions are timeboxed and require an override audit entry. For private deployments, a feature toggle will enable local audit forwarding to customer Kinesis/ELK endpoints.
migration_steps: Create DB migration for flag table with scope columns and versioning
Add read-only defaults for existing orgs (flags default to false/no-blocking)
Backfill existing public links to include origin metadata to support mass-removal
Deploy config service event emitter behind feature gate, enable for internal telemetry first
Roll RBAC v2 permission checks in console and API incrementally (view -> modify)
Announce to customers and provide opt-in window before hard enforcement for exports
rollout_plan: Week 1: Internal dogfood in staging; surface audit events to internal SLO dashboard
Week 2: Beta release to 10 pilot customers with compliance teams; collect feedback
Week 3: Gradual tenant enablement (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary gating on blocked-export rates
Emergency rollback path: toggle enforcement to ‘audit-only’ to stop blocking while keeping logs
Post-launch: 30-day review to evaluate false positives and UX clarity
QA_tests: Verify audit entries for toggle changes include user id, role, IP, and reason field
Simulate export job triggered by admin and by non-admin user while data_offboard_lock enabled
Attempt to create public link as owner when public_link_block is enabled -> expect 403 and audit event
Network ACL enforcement: validate API calls from allowed CIDR succeed and blocked CIDR fail
RBAC matrix test: ensure view-only role cannot modify toggles or create exceptions
Integration test across hosted/dedicated/private with audit ingestion endpoint mocked
audit_log_entries: TOGGLE_CHANGE: {actor, actor_role, org_id, toggle_name, old_value, new_value, reason, request_id}
EXPORT_BLOCKED: {actor, org_id, export_job_id, rule_matched, timestamp, request_id}
NETWORK_ACCESS_ALERT: {source_ip, org_id, requested_resource, acl_id, action_taken, timestamp}
SSO_SAML_notes: When SSO is enabled, admin actions must log SAML principal information (assertion id and issuer) in audit events. For IdP-initiated flows where user email differs, persist and surface both asserted_identity and local_user_id in logs. Enforce session re-authn for toggle changes if the last SSO assertion is older than configurable TTL (default 12 hours).
RBAC_v2_mapping: compliance.view_flags -> can view state and history of compliance toggles
compliance.change_flags -> can modify toggles and create exceptions (audit reason required)
compliance.override_window -> can create timeboxed exceptions (records approver and duration)
compliance.view_audit -> can view audit events related to flags

notes: PM and Legal reviewed the policy language; Legal requested an audit reason field and retention policy >= 2 years. Design provided copy variants A/B to clarify consequences of enabling each toggle. Engineering flagged a potential race between export worker and cache invalidation — mitigating with optimistic version check on worker start. Follow-ups: (1) define retention in infra-logs; (2) add customer-facing migration guide; (3) draft runbook for false positive incidents.
